name: Veldtmann RadCore Reactor Zone Enclosure Suit
description:
A Tier 3 radiation enclosure suit for reactor maintenance and contaminated Shelf zones. The outer shell is dense lead-composite polyfilm in matte institutional yellow, stenciled with Veldtmann's black chevron and dosimeter attachment points at chest, wrist, and collar. Inner layers are triple-sealed with radiation-dampening aerogel batting and a moisture barrier.

The integrated helmet is hard-shelled polycarb with a leaded-glass visor. All seams are pressure-bonded and color-coded for inspection — red seams indicate primary radiation barriers. Rated RAD-IV for gamma and beta exposure.
functionality: RAD-IV rated for gamma and beta shielding up to 6-hour exposure windows. Dosimeter ports at three points allow continuous monitoring. Pressure-bonded seams prevent particulate ingress. Integrated air supply runs 90 minutes. Leaded visor maintains visibility in high-flux environments.
what_it_says: Someone who goes into the places the rest of the city pretends don't exist.
story_hooks: A suit returned from a Shelf contamination zone registered exposure levels that would require the area to be restricted — but no official restriction was ever filed.
The dosimeter on a reactor worker's suit has been spoofed to read low; someone doesn't want the actual exposure logged.
Veldtmann quietly recalled this batch number two months ago but never collected the suits already distributed to Shelf contractors.

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian full-body enclosure suit with an integrated hard helmet, presenting a bulky, technical silhouette. The institutional yellow outer shell dominates the visual impression, marked with stark black Veldtmann chevrons and visible attachment points. The suit reads as industrial and purposeful—designed for function over form, with the rigid helmet creating an almost alien presence.
physical_description.fit: Oversized and loose-fitting throughout the torso and limbs, with sealed compression cuffs at wrists and ankles. The suit accommodates layering beneath and allows restricted mobility in exchange for maximum protection. The helmet sits flush with shoulder seals, creating a monolithic upper profile.
physical_description.primary_material: Dense lead-composite polyfilm (outer shell), triple-sealed radiation-dampening aerogel batting (middle layer), moisture barrier (inner), hard polycarb with leaded-glass visor (helmet)
physical_description.texture: Matte, slightly ribbed polyfilm exterior with a dull institutional finish. Pressure-bonded seams create subtle linear texture across the suit. The visor has a faint amber tint from lead-glass, creating a subtle reflective quality. All surfaces designed for easy decontamination.
physical_description.color_scheme: Institutional matte yellow (#D4C51A) as primary, with high-contrast black Veldtmann chevrons stenciled across chest and back. Red pressure-bonded seams trace critical radiation barriers along shoulders, spine, and limb joints. The visor interior amber-tinted from leaded glass.
physical_description.closures: Heavy-duty magnetic seals at neck, wrists, and ankles. Central front placket with friction-fit locking mechanism and pressure-bonded overlap seams for airtight integrity. Helmet locks via three-point magnetic coupling to suit collar.
distinctive_features: Integrated hard polycarb helmet with leaded-glass visor
Three dosimeter attachment points (chest, wrist, collar) with reinforced Φ-rated mounting tabs
Color-coded seams—red for primary radiation barriers, standard black for secondary
Veldtmann black chevron company logo stenciled across chest and back
Pressure-bonded seams throughout for inspection visibility
Stenciled RAD-IV certification marking and inspection date stamps on left thigh
Reinforced articulation panels at elbows, knees, and groin for increased protection in high-exposure zones
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 functional corporate equipment—standardized safety gear for working-class industrial maintenance personnel employed by corpo subsidiaries
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by reactor maintenance workers, contaminated zone salvagers, and sub-level infrastructure personnel. Signals employment in hazardous corporate infrastructure roles. The suit implies exposure to unstable Shelf zones or legacy nuclear facilities—not casual streetwear but recognizable and respected among industrial workers.
physical_description.condition_typical: Usually worn with visible dosimeter wear marks, minor paint scuffs on the yellow exterior from industrial handling, and faint radiation-detection tape residue at seams. The suit is periodically pressure-tested; successful tests leave visible inspection stamps. Most units show 3-5 years of weathered use despite being regularly decontaminated.
